title: Evaluation-normalized scalar Hom comparison for a site-perfect first variable
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme with a small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and let $R\to S$ be a map of sheaves of commutative rings on that site. Use the unbounded module-sheaf derived categories $D(R),D(S)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], derived change of rings $F=-\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}S$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], and derived internal Hom $H_R,H_S$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Let $P\in D(R)$ be site-perfect: locally on every site object it is represented by a bounded complex of direct summands of finite free $R$-module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-strict-perfect-coefficient-package]. For every $Q\in D(R)$ the canonical morphism
$$c_{P,Q}:F H_R(P,Q)\longrightarrow H_S(FP,FQ)$$
is an isomorphism, natural in both variables. Here $c_{P,Q}$ is defined by tensor-Hom adjunction as the transpose of
$$FP\otimes_S^{\mathbf L}F H_R(P,Q)\xrightarrow{\sim}F(P\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}H_R(P,Q))\xrightarrow{F(\operatorname{ev}_{P,Q})}FQ,$$
using the canonical tensor comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. Thus this specified map preserves evaluation. No flatness of $S$ over $R$, or boundedness, constructibility or finite Tor-amplitude condition on $Q$, is assumed.

proof.text: Regard $R\to S$ as the structural ring map of the identity geometric morphism of the sheaf topos. Its module pullback is scalar extension, so its total derived pullback is the functor $F$ in the statement, computed on K-flat representatives [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Equip $D(R),D(S)$ with the canonical closed symmetric monoidal structures [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal]. The canonical comparisons of [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons], specialized to this ringed-topos morphism, make $F$ strong monoidal, with tensorator the inverse of the displayed pullback-tensor comparison. In particular this is the actual comparison used in the definition of $c_{P,Q}$, and its unit identifies $F(R)$ with $S$.

proof.text: Put $D=H_R(P,R)$ and let $e:P\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}D\to R$ be coefficient evaluation in the stated tensor order, that is, the evaluation $H_R(P,R)\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}P\to R$ of [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal] precomposed with the symmetry $\sigma_{P,D}$. Use on $D(R)$ (and likewise on $D(S)$) the bijections $\operatorname{Hom}(P\otimes A,B)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(A\otimes P,B)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(A,H_R(P,B))$ obtained from the closed structure of [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal] by precomposing with the symmetry; they are natural in all three variables, and under them evaluation $\operatorname{ev}_{P,N}:P\otimes H_R(P,N)\to N$ is the counit composed with $\sigma$. For $N\in D(R)$ let $\phi_N:D\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}N\to H_R(P,N)$ be the transpose of $P\otimes(D\otimes N)\cong(P\otimes D)\otimes N\xrightarrow{e\otimes1_N}R\otimes N\cong N$. By [lem-sfb-ringed-site-duality-maps] the canonical comparison $e_{P,N}:N\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}D\to H_R(P,N)$ is the internal composition $H_R(R,N)\otimes H_R(P,R)\to H_R(P,N)$ after $N\cong H_R(R,N)$, and internal composition is the transpose of the composite of the two evaluations [def-coef-ringed-tensor-hom-model]. Transposing $e_{P,N}\circ\sigma_{D,N}$ and using naturality of the adjunction bijection, the hexagon identity and the unit isomorphism $N\cong H_R(R,N)$ (whose transpose is the unitor), its transpose is the displayed map $(e\otimes1_N)$ up to the associator and unitor; hence $\phi_N=e_{P,N}\circ\sigma_{D,N}$. Perfectness of $P$ is exactly the local bounded finite-free-retract hypothesis of [lem-sfb-ringed-site-perfect-duality], whose canonical evaluation comparison $D\otimes^{\mathbf L}_RN\to H_R(P,N)$ is this map $e_{P,N}\circ\sigma_{D,N}$; that theorem makes it an isomorphism for every $N\in D(R)$. So every $\phi_N$ is an isomorphism. These assertions apply to all unbounded $N$; no tensor-Hom isomorphism other than the transpose of $e\otimes 1_N$ is chosen.

proof.text: Apply [lem-fix-closed-evaluation-dual-criterion] to these actual evaluation comparisons. Its coevaluation is $c=\phi_P^{-1}u_P:R\to D\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}P$, where $u_P$ transposes $1_P$. Both triangle identities follow from that criterion. Thus $P$ has an exact dual pair with $D$ in the canonical monoidal structure, with evaluation equal to the evaluation used in defining the scalar Hom map.

proof.text: Apply [lem-fix-monoidal-dual-hom-comparison] with $G=F$, the strong monoidal structure from step 1, and the dual pair from step 3. It gives an isomorphism $F H_R(P,Q)\to H_S(FP,FQ)$ for every $Q\in D(R)$. Its defining transpose is precisely $F(\operatorname{ev}_{P,Q})\circ\mu_{P,H_R(P,Q)}$, which is the transpose specified in the item. Bijectivity of the tensor-Hom adjunction therefore identifies this isomorphism with $c_{P,Q}$ itself.

proof.text: The evaluation identity is the inverse-transpose equation: $\operatorname{ev}_{FP,FQ}\circ(1_{FP}\otimes c_{P,Q})=F(\operatorname{ev}_{P,Q})\circ\mu_{P,H_R(P,Q)}$. For $a:P'\to P$ and $b:Q\to Q'$, transpose the two maps from $F H_R(P,Q)$ to $H_S(FP',FQ')$. Naturality of evaluation and of $\mu$ makes both transposes $F(b\circ\operatorname{ev}_{P,Q}\circ(a\otimes1))\circ\mu_{P',H_R(P,Q)}$. Hence $H_S(Fa,Fb)c_{P,Q}=c_{P',Q'}F(H_R(a,b))$. This proves both naturalities and preservation of the specified evaluation. None of the preceding statements requires flatness of $S$ or any finiteness or boundedness assumption on $Q$.
